packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
PACKET-05 - UNVERIFIED IMAGE READING (blind; no outside source consulted, no identification attempted)

Exposure note: none from outside the images. The codex page on the left carries its own explicit
rubric (transcribed below as visible text); I did not use it or anything else to supply readings.

1. LAYOUT SURVEY (observation)
- image-001 and image-006 are two overviews of the same opening (image-006 has the gutter opened
  slightly further, showing two more lines of the right-hand leaf and a narrow strip of a further
  leaf/stub in the gutter with line-ends in reddish ink).
- RIGHT: a parchment leaf used as pastedown/flyleaf inside the back board, turned 90 degrees
  (its lines run vertically in the overview, top of text toward the fore-edge). Single column,
  long lines, large well-spaced Caroline minuscule in dark brown-black ink, 19 full lines
  visible plus part of a 20th running into the gutter. No rubric, no coloured initial; sentence
  openings marked by slightly enlarged plain capitals (U, C, I, A, N, E, Q). Punctuation by
  point and by point-with-comma. Abbreviation strokes on "p̄positio", "-t(ur)" as a 2-shaped sign
  above t. One Greek word written in capitals with a wavy line above it (line 11). One
  superscript correction ("raro", o written above with expunction dot, line 12). Underline-like
  stroke under "Loco" (line 3) - may be a later pen mark. Marginal note in the outer margin
  beside line 5: "Deten;" (small capitals-like hand). Modern pencil "A" at the upper-left corner
  of the leaf (as rotated) / "D" at the top-right corner of the board in the overview. Prickings
  visible down the margin. Stains and small holes at the head.
- LEFT: last written page of the codex itself (upright), single column of smaller Caroline
  minuscule in brown ink: 11 lines of prose ending "... amen", an erased line, an explicit in
  mixed capitals, four verse lines, and then a mass of pen-trials, names and neumed incipits in
  several hands and inks, with further erased lines of large display capitals showing through.
  Two interlinear glosses in the prose (line 8). An ink drawing/smudge in the outer margin.
- Tentative interpretation: the right-hand leaf is a fragment from a different book (grammatical
  prose with quoted verse examples), reused in the binding; the left page is the host volume.

2. AREAS SELECTED / UNREAD
Read: the whole visible text of the reused leaf (image-002/003, repeated in image-007/008 which
add the 20th line); the prose and verses on the codex page (image-004); the more legible
pen-trials (image-004/005). Unread: erased display-capital lines on the left page; the gutter
strip in image-006 (only line-ends, too small); the hidden side of the pasted leaf.

3. TRANSCRIPTION

A. Reused leaf (right). Each line runs across image-002 (left part) and image-003 (right part);
the crops overlap in the middle. Line numbers are the same counted from the top of either image
(image-007/008 repeat them identically).

L18 "ut p(er)currit": the first letters are "utp" with a stroke through p.

B. Codex page (left), upright - image-004

4. LIMITATIONS
- Section A is clear and I am confident of it letter by letter except where marked (L6 "genet?i",
  L15 "om(ne)s", the margin note, L20 which is cut by the gutter). The text begins and ends
  mid-sentence; the leaf is evidently trimmed or its continuation is hidden under the gutter.
- Word division in A and B follows sense where the scribe runs words together; spelling kept.
- Section C is a set of unrelated jottings; readings of names and of L7, L9, L10 are doubtful.
- The gutter strip visible in image-006 and the erased capitals were not read; a flatter opening
  or a separate shot of the stub would be needed.
